summary: Extend the memory-policy surface to add a telegram-conversation durability class (30-day retention) and two new tags (#telegram, #digest) to the canonical tag taxonomy.
rationale: The existing memory-policy has two durability classes (transient: 7 days, persistent: 90 days). Telegram conversation turns have a different lifecycle — longer than transient but shorter than general persistent memories, and they need to be identifiable as bot-sourced. Without a dedicated class, every conversation turn either expires in 7 days (losing useful context) or pollutes the persistent class (adding noise to Xavier's personal knowledge base). Adding #telegram and #digest tags keeps Telegram-sourced entries distinguishable in audits and synthesis.
evidence_refs: docs/companion-agent/brewmind-companion-contract.md — Section B (Ephemeral vs Canonical memory tiers)
proposed_diff_summary: Add to memory-policy/policy.json durability_classes.classes: telegram-conversation (description: 'Telegram bot conversation turns and exchanges. Bot-sourced, session-scoped but cross-session relevant.', retention_days: 30, eligible_for_synthesis: true, auto_archive: false, promotion_path: 'evidence/ → prepared-context/synthesis/ → proposal → governed-state'). Add to tag_taxonomy.tags: #telegram ('Any entry captured from a Telegram bot conversation') and #digest ('Daily digest content generated and sent by the proactivity scheduler').
